4.DEPRESSION
-During pregnancy 12%
-3 months PP = 13%
-1-year after delivery = 15 – 20%
-Past history and FH es risk 42%
-Bipolar depression – risk of psychosis.

Diagnostic key words:

• Lack of interest in friends, life, baby
• Persistent sadness low mood
• Don’t improve but worse with time
•Fatigue or low energy.
•Worthlessness and hopelessness

 

Associated symptoms:

•Sleep disturbance
•Indecisiveness
•Poor or ed appetite
•Suicidal thoughts
•Agitation or slowing of movements
•Guilt or self-blame
•Impaired social or occupational activities
•Poor concentration
•Low self-confidence.

Post – partum depression:

Onset: 1st 2weeks after birth

2 peak presentations

1 @ 2 – 4weeks pp

2nd @ 10 – 14weeks pp

•FH + Personal History of depression = 42%

Postnatal depression

Greatest at 6 – 8weeks.

•Only personal depression = 15% chance of PP depression.
•Risk of recurrence in future pregnancies 1:2 – 1:3

 

Depression Screening:

1.Feeling down, hopeless, depressed over month

2.Lack of interest over past month

 

1 Or 2 positives

 

Full assessment by

Edinberg Postnatal Scale

Or

Patient health Questionnaire

Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems:

•Little interest or pleasure in doing things?
•Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?
•Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much?
•Feeling tired or having little energy?
•Poor appetite or overeating?
•Feeling bad about yourself – or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down?
•Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television?
•Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed?
•Or the opposite – being so uneasy or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual?
•Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself in some way?

Rating:

•Not at all: 0
•Several days: 1
•More than half the days: 2
•Nearly every day: 3

Depression severity

•0–4: none
•5–9: mild
•10–14: moderate
•15–19: moderately severe
•20–27: severe

Fetomaternal Consequences of Depression:

Mother:

•Relapse
•Poor nutrition
•Suicide
•Drug abuse
•Postnatal depression

Baby:

•Abortion
•Pre term birth
•LBW
•Low APGAR
•NICU admission
•Breast feeding problems

Management:

⇨Women not taking any treatment or newly diagnose

1. Mild – Moderate:

 

Refer to

•Local psychology services
•Primary care mental health

 

⇨Low intensity CBT
-9 – 12weeks therapy
-6 – 8 min sessions face to face or telephonic
-30 – 60min session
-Every week or fortnightly

 

2. Moderate- Severe:

•High intensity CBT
•Pharmacological treatment

SSRI

SNRI

TCA

In case she declines CBT, or CBT is ineffective.

•Combination of CBT and medications if alone CBT or medications are not effective.
•Severe Depression:

Catatonic features, psychotic features

•Switch antidepressants if already taking or
•Augmentation treatment with antipsychotic or mood stabilizers.
•ECT – in severe or life-threatening conditions.

•SSRI
